assembly_notes: Entryway hall tree with a flip-top bench. One rigid carcass root carries both side cheeks, the cabinet bottom, the rear seat ledgers and the tall tower back between the cheeks. The bench slab is a separate part hinged REVOLUTE about +x along its rear edge on two knuckle pairs that sit on the ledgers, so the flip is the fixed category motion. lower_build fills the carcass under the seat: drawer_bank cuts a face frame into bay_count bays and puts one PRISMATIC drawer in each; door_cabinet closes the whole opening with one overlay door on a vertical REVOLUTE axis over a fixed interior shelf; seat_bin walls the opening into a well with no independent moving storage. upper_build treats the tower above the seat: open_cubbies adds a cubby floor, top and bay_count-1 dividers; mirror_panel closes the field with glass in an applied surround divided by bay_count-1 muntins; hook_rail crosses the field with a rail carrying bay_count hooks; framed_board applies a stile-and-rail frame with bay_count recessed fields. case_dress is how the case meets the floor and the ceiling: stepped_plinth_crown steps a broad plinth out on all four sides under a two-piece crown, toe_kick_rail recesses a front-only kick board under the case and finishes with one thin flush crown rail plus applied front stiles, flush_base_crown keeps the base flush with the carcass under a single broad deep crown. Every case_dress bridges the cheek bottoms to the floor and the cheek tops to the tower back, so all three combine with every lower_build and upper_build. bay_count is the multiplicity and is read by both builds on the same pitch. carcass_width_m, carcass_depth_m, seat_height_m and tower_height_m are the independent parameters; paint palette, pull profile and moulding depth are non-core.
